messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing intermittent failures for model-pulser jobs in us-west-2? Started ~08:03 with connect timeouts to the internal proxy (vpce-0a1b2c3d).
vikram: Yea, I noticed timeouts too. I pulled a few DNS responses and they include ENI IPs from different AZs, clients sometimes pick a remote AZ IP -> cross-AZ egress via NAT.
sam: Confirmed on the NAT metrics — us-west-2a NAT GW hit high connection count around 08:04 and we saw SNAT port exhaustion on a couple hosts. This matches cross-AZ egress pattern.
jess: Can you paste the dig/nslookup you saw? Also check Route53 private zone — any weird records or CNAMEs?
vikram: Here's a quick dig I ran from a broken host:
```
dig +short vpce-0a1b2c3d-xxxx.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com
# output (example)
10.0.12.45   # eni in us-west-2b
10.10.4.8    # eni in us-west-2a
10.2.3.6     # eni in us-west-2c
```
sam: That explains it. If the resolver returns the AZ-local IP last, the client may still bind to the first IP it sees (or keep a cached socket) and traffic gets NATted across AZ. If NAT in the chosen AZ is overloaded, connections drop.
maria: I also found nscd running on some instances with default cache TTL 3600s, so even after ENI rotation clients kept the stale IP.
jess: Route53 private zone is just the default VPC endpoint private dns (no custom CNAMEs). TTL for the record is 300s, but local host resolver + nscd overrides that.
sam: Short term mitigation:
- flush local DNS cache on workers (`sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved` or `sudo systemctl restart nscd`)
- restart affected app workers so sockets re-resolve
- temporarily increase NAT GW capacity / add small autoscaling for NAT allocation
I already bumped NAT capacity for 2h.
vikram: Long term options:
- make app DNS behavior AZ-aware (prefer endpoint IPs that match instance AZ)
- reduce local DNS cache TTL or configure nscd/systemd-resolved to respect DNS TTLs
- run a small sidecar that picks the AZ-local ENI IP and rewrites host resolution
- ensure SGs allow ephemeral egress to endpoint ENIs so fallback paths aren't blocked
jess: Filed INFRA-724 with the runbook and follow-ups: reduce host cache TTL, add AZ-affinity guidance to the client lib, and validate SG egress rules for endpoint ENIs.
deploy-bot: NAT-capacity-update: increased nat-gw fleet by +1 in us-west-2a at 08:15 (ticket INFRA-723).
maria: After flushing caches + NAT bump the model-pulser success rate is back to ~98%. Leaving the NAT bump for 2h then we'll roll back once things look stable. Thanks all :thumbsup:
sam: Suggest we add a short health-check that looks for cross-AZ DNS bindings and alerts when skew > 20% so we catch this earlier.
jess: Will add that to INFRA-724. Closing the immediate incident but keeping the runbook open for follow-ups.
